text:
anya: Heads-up — noticed oscillations in region-penalty signals when the route-evict path kicks in. Seeing repeated attach/detach on a few edge routes after ~2m spikes. want a quick sync on smoothing vs explicit eviction controls.

mike: Can you paste the policy snippet you used and an example timeline?

anya: pasted the minimal config we applied to the canary tenant: 
```
policy {
  region_penalty(window=60s, decay=0.2, min=0.0, max=1.0)
  eviction {
    threshold=0.8
    grace=120s  # wait before evicting once threshold crossed
    cooldown=300s # no re-evict for this window
  }
}
```
Behavior: latency spikes 30-90s -> penalty climbs fast -> eviction triggers after grace -> a few minutes later latency drops -> penalty falls -> route gets reinstated -> cycle repeats.

mike: This is classic feedback oscillation. My quick take: use EWMA smoothing + hysteresis + require sustained signal across 2 independent windows. e.g. 
```
# EWMA
s_t = alpha * x_t + (1-alpha) * s_{t-1}  # alpha ~ 0.1-0.2 for 60s samples
# eviction condition
if short_ewma > short_thr and long_ewma > long_thr and s_t > eviction_threshold: evict
```
Set cooldown > 2*sampling to avoid thrash.

rachel: Agree with smoothing, but watch out: autoscaler reads raw latency/queue_length. if routing uses smoothed metric and autoscaler uses raw, we can end up under-provisioning when a real sustained load appears. We should keep scaling signals untouched or derive separate metrics for scaling vs routing.

samir: +1. Also suggest split signal into: spike_score (fast window) and drift_score (long window). Eviction requires both. That handles transient infra blips. Example: 
```
spike = EWMA(alpha=0.3, window=30s)
drift = EWMA(alpha=0.05, window=10m)
if spike > spike_thr AND drift > drift_thr: evict
else if spike > spike_thr: prefer degrade-route (lower weight) but do not evict
```
so we can avoid hard evict when only spike present.

deploy-bot: :information_source: Canary policy applied to tenant-id:canary-42 at 2026-03-20T14:05Z — monitoring window active. Link: https://console/redwood/canaries/42

yiming: Would love a sim harness before landing this. Small sim catches a lot of these oscillations. We should: 1) replay traces (p95 bursts), 2) run 10k-sample montecarlo with random spike patterns, 3) measure false-evict rate. We should also add a metric: evictions_per_1000_requests.

anya: Good call. Also need to quantify telemetry cost — more EWMA windows = more series. Mike, Samir — you want to own the RFC + sim plan? I'll add ops and autoscaler folks as reviewers.

mike: I can take RFC + initial sim harness. Will sketch config options (alpha, windows, thresholds, cooldowns) + compatibility notes for autoscaler.

samir: I'll help on the sim scenarios and add a test that runs against the policy-sandbox. Also propose a small feature: `route_state = degraded|evicted|normal` to make downstream consumers (autoscaler/console) explicit.

anya: Perfect. Action items: Mike open RFC today (link in thread), Samir add sim traces, Rachel to validate autoscaler separation, Yiming to verify metrics we need. We'll test on canary for 48h before rolling. :thumbsup:

mike: One tiny perf note — computing multiple EWMA windows per route at 100k rps means we should pre-aggregate samples by shard and compute at 1s cadence. I'll put a perf estimate in RFC.

rachel: If sim looks good, propose adding a togglable feature-flag so SRE can revert immediate evict behavior without deploy.

anya: Sounds good. Thanks all.
